name: Shrimp and Sausage Gumbo
description: This recipe is a simplified version of AB’s Seafood Gumbo .

ingredients.name: Cajun or Creole Seasoning
ingredients.originalText: 1 tbsp Cajun or Creole Seasoning (Creole Kick)

ingredients.name: Instead of chicken broth, you can use your own shrimp stock
ingredients.originalText: (Optional) Instead of chicken broth, you can use your own shrimp stock

instructions.text: Read the entire method first and measure the following ingredients before turning on the heat: 2-3 lbs Shrimp; 2 lbs Andouille Sausage; 2 (32 oz) Chicken Broth; 1 cup olive oil; 1 cup All Purpose Flour; 1 cup finely chopped Yellow Onion; 1 cup finely chopped Green Pepper; 1 cup finely chopped Celery; 2 tbsp minced Garlic; 1 tbsp Worcestershire Sauce; 1 tbsp Cajun or Creole Seasoning (Creole Kick); 1 12 oz. bottle of Beer; 1 tsp dried Thyme; 1 tsp dried Parsley; 3 - 5 Bay Leafs; 1/2 cup Green Onions; 1-2 cups White Rice; (Optional) 1 Jalapeño Pepper; (Optional) Instead of chicken broth, you can use your own shrimp stock. Keep ingredients marked optional separate until their step.

Prepare these ingredients before cooking: Garlic: minced. Wash produce under running water before cutting. Use a cutting board and a sharp knife; keep raw meat and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.
Prep the vegetables
Get the roux started: Mix oil and flour over heat until it turns into a dark chocolate color.
Low - medium heat for about 30 minutes or medium - high for 15 - 20 minutes if you’re feeling brave.
Ensure to stir frequently while adding the following ingredients.
Add onion.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Add celery and peppers.
Cook for 5 minutes.
Add garlic.
Cook for 1 minute.
Add beer.
Add broth.
Add seasonings and Worcestershire Sauce.
Add sausage and bring to a boil.
Lower heat, cover, simmer for 90 minutes. A simmer means small, gentle bubbles; lower the burner if it boils vigorously.
Increase heat to medium.
Add shrimp and cook for 5-7 minutes.
Turn off the heat and serve over white rice.
(Optional) For leftovers, boil gumbo with dry white rice and turn it into a jambalaya.

Before serving, insert a food thermometer into the thickest piece of chicken or turkey, away from bone: it must reach 165°F (74°C). If using already-cooked poultry, reheat it to 165°F (74°C). Continue cooking and recheck if needed; wash hands and utensils after handling raw poultry and do not rinse it.

Turn off any burners or oven when cooking is finished. Follow the cooling or resting instruction above before cutting or serving. Serve the finished dish as directed; allow hot portions to cool enough to eat.

source.author: Carl Zimmerman
